clue.text: Memory containing nothing? That'll make you ramble

indicators.note: the word for memory holds the letter for nothing inside it

parts.note: RAM is computer memory (random access memory)
O, the zero shape, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A rambling mind that has emptied its memory sets off wandering.
explanation.definitionFit: To roam is to wander about aimlessly, which is what rambling means as a verb.

clue.text: Fast pace heading for home for us? Not at this time!

definitions.text: Fast pace heading for home for us? Not at this time!

parts.note: a rush is a burst of fast pace

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, here taken from home

parts.note: something for us is ours, giving OUR

explanation.surface: Commuters dream of a quick dash home, but are told it won't happen just now.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the period when crowded roads and trains make a fast journey home impossible.
explanation.definitionFit: The busiest commuting period is exactly when a speedy trip home is out of the question.

clue.text: It'll account for all corrosion initially found on one sewer

definitions.text: It'll account for all corrosion initially found on one sewer

indicators.note: takes the opening letters of the words all and corrosion

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
a drain is a sewer, a channel carrying away waste water

explanation.surface: An engineer blames the rusting of a sewer on some single cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found on' places the first pieces above the rest in this down clue. The whole clue also describes polluted rainfall that eats into metal and stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Polluted rainfall containing acids is a well-known cause of corrosion of buildings and metalwork.

clue.text: Besotted lad married one with the brains of a butterfly

definitions.text: one with the brains of a butterfly

indicators.note: someone besotted is muddled, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A lovestruck young groom is mocked as having no more sense than a butterfly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with the brains of a butterfly' sounds like an insult for a scatterbrain, but the definition really means something that is a butterfly.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common European butterfly species, so it certainly has a butterfly's brain.

clue.text: Woman embraced by Greek?

indicators.note: the name sits inside the longer word, so its outer letters are dropped

parts.note: a Hellene is a Greek

explanation.surface: A woman is hugged by a Greek man.
explanation.walkthrough: The name lies within HELLENE, a word for a Greek; removing its first and last letters H and E leaves it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellen is a woman's first name, so any woman might bear it.

clue.text: Prove sectarian to be mistaken

indicators.note: letters that are mistaken are put in the wrong order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to show that a sectarian person is in the wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascertain something is to establish it as certain, much as one proves a fact.

clue.text: It might allow you to grab the lead, going through the field

definitions.text: It might allow you to grab the lead, going through the field

parts.words: It might allow you to grab the lead, going through the field
parts.note: reads like a sporting move to take the lead past the field, but describes a device sweeping a field for buried lead

explanation.surface: A runner surges through the field to take the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' is the metal, not first place, and 'field' is farmland, not the other competitors.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobbyist's sweeping device beeps over buried metal such as lead as it is carried across farmland.

clue.text: Property legally, one divorced from actual existence

indicators.note: one letter is separated off from the longer word

parts.note: reality is actual existence
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A divorce lawyer weighs property against the hard facts of life.
explanation.definitionFit: Realty is the legal term for real property such as land and buildings.

clue.text: Mean to fib initially, then go into hiding

indicators.note: says the fib comes first, ahead of the word for mean

parts.note: to fib is to lie
low can mean mean, as in a low trick

explanation.surface: Someone means to tell a small lie first and then disappear.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie low is an idiom for keeping out of sight, staying hidden.

clue.text: Capable Silk led astray? Corrupted, nothing less

indicators.note: letters led astray wander out of order, so they are rearranged
the letter for nothing is taken away from the word

parts.note: foul can mean corrupted or polluted
O, the zero shape, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A capable Queen's Counsel (a 'silk') is lured into corruption.
explanation.walkthrough: SILK rearranged gives SKIL; FOUL without its O leaves FUL. A 'silk' is a senior barrister in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilful person is able and expert, which is what capable means.

clue.text: Musical effect? It's not true!

definitions.meaning: a clash in harmony where a note and its chromatically altered form appear in different parts
read literally, a lying account or untrue story told

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a music-theory term for a harmonic clash, and literally an untrue telling.

clue.text: Bed time after time seen in small house

indicators.note: the first named time is placed after the second

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
an age is a long period of time
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Bedtime comes round again and again in a little house.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottage is a small, usually rural, dwelling.

clue.text: Doctrinaire type cut short expression of commiseration, right?

indicators.note: the last letter of the phrase is lopped off

parts.note: hard lines is a British expression meaning bad luck

explanation.surface: A dogmatic person rudely interrupts someone's sympathy, asking if that's right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard lines!' is British slang for 'bad luck!'; without its final S it gives HARDLINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardliner sticks rigidly to a doctrine or policy, as a doctrinaire person does.

clue.text: Auction item no longer open? It's a chancy business

parts.note: each item sold at auction is a lot
a door pushed to is closed, so to means no longer open

explanation.surface: An auction lot has closed bidding, which was a gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' as in 'push the door to' means shut.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a lottery game, a business of pure chance.

clue.text: Football team sets forth for country

parts.note: many British football clubs are called United, such as Manchester United
to state is to set forth in words

explanation.surface: A football club lays out its plans for the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The United States is a country in North America.

clue.text: Big name is finally active over dubious arrest

indicators.note: takes the last letter of the word is

parts.note: up means active, as in up and about

indicators.note: a dubious arrest is suspect, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A celebrity is back in action after a questionable arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: In this down clue 'over' places S and UP above ERSTAR, the rearranged ARREST.
explanation.definitionFit: A superstar is a very famous person, a big name in show business or sport.

clue.text: Team's effrontery is a move in the wrong direction

definitions.text: a move in the wrong direction

parts.note: a team is a side, and the possessive adds S
lip is cheeky talk or effrontery

explanation.surface: A team's cheek is judged a step backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideslip is a sideways skid, movement off the intended direction, as of a car or plane.

clue.text: Way to include playing of Arne in Prom?

indicators.note: the abbreviation for way takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: playing the words means rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: A conductor finds a way to fit some Arne into the Proms concerts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prom' suggests the London Proms concerts, and Arne is the English composer of Rule, Britannia!, sung at the Last Night; but here it is a promenade. OF ARNE rearranged gives EAFRON.
explanation.definitionFit: A prom, short for promenade, is a walkway along the shore of a seaside town.

clue.text: Wait for an answer

parts.note: reads as an instruction to be patient, but names the delay before a reply arrives

explanation.surface: Someone is told to be patient until a reply comes.
explanation.definitionFit: The interval between a request and its reply is the wait for an answer.

clue.text: Endless expense on doctors to become whole

indicators.note: the word loses its final letter

parts.note: cost is expense
MO is a medical officer, a doctor; plural MOs

explanation.surface: Unlimited spending on medics aims to make a patient well.
explanation.definitionFit: The cosmos is the universe considered as an ordered whole.

clue.text: Cloth's excellent, almost plush

parts.note: fab is slang for fabulous, excellent

indicators.note: the word is not quite complete, losing its last letter

parts.note: rich can mean plush or luxurious

explanation.surface: A fabric is praised as fine and nearly luxurious.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric is woven or knitted material, that is cloth.

clue.text: Exclamation about American backing given to a US city

indicators.note: the exclamation goes around the other piece

parts.note: oh is an exclamation

indicators.note: the abbreviation is read backwards

explanation.surface: A cry of support for an American goes out to a city in the States.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha is the largest city in Nebraska, in the USA.

clue.text: Dish that's best afore cooking?

indicators.note: cooking the letters reworks them into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A dish is said to be at its finest before it is cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'best afore' recalls a 'best before' date on food, misleading towards freshness.
explanation.definitionFit: Roast beef is a classic meat dish, especially a traditional English one.

clue.text: A daughter college let in

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: A college admits a daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit someone is to let them in, as through a door.

clue.text: Football teams in market for left-winger

indicators.note: the teams are placed inside the market

parts.note: a mart is a market
a team of eleven is an XI, in Roman numerals; plural XIs

explanation.surface: Football clubs in the transfer market hunt for a left winger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left-winger' sounds like a football position, but means a political leftist.
explanation.definitionFit: A Marxist follows Karl Marx's socialist ideas and so sits on the political left.

clue.text: Cherry extra lovely at the outset — look at that!

parts.note: more means extra

indicators.note: takes the first letter of the word lovely

parts.note: lo is an old exclamation meaning look

explanation.surface: Someone admires an extra fine cherry at first sight.
explanation.definitionFit: The morello is a sour dark-red variety of cherry.

clue.text: Alternative tariff is not so good

parts.note: a second is an alternative choice
a rate is a tariff or charge

explanation.surface: Customers complain that the alternative pricing plan is worse.
explanation.definitionFit: Something second-rate is inferior, of lesser quality.

clue.text: Drunkard without pressure having a small amount

indicators.note: in the old sense outside, the drunkard's word surrounds the letter

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard

explanation.surface: A drunk under no pressure has just a little drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot of something is a small amount, as in a spot of lunch.
